query: Why do some agents have longer resolution times?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Directly the dependent variable for the query (resolution time), so highly useful in principle. But values are unsound: many negative hours and figures not reconcilable with the timestamps shown (closed_at equals sys_updated_on, opened_at not reflected). The produced numbers appear miscomputed/invented rather than a valid closed-minus-opened span.

per_column.name: priority_numeric
per_column.rationale: A numeric encoding of the existing priority column gives a clean axis to group/model resolution time against. Largely redundant with the original priority but adds modeling leverage; values are a sound reading of the source.

per_column.name: category_type
per_column.rationale: Rolls category into higher-level buckets (Infrastructure/Software/Other), a reasonable grouping axis for comparing resolution times. Mappings shown (database, VPN, intranet -> Infrastructure; software update -> Software) are sound categorisations of the source text.

per_column.name: is_critical
per_column.rationale: A binary flag derived from priority (=1 for priority 1). Grounded and consistent (88 criticals match 88 priority-1 rows), but largely a restatement of priority_numeric, giving limited new analytical leverage.

per_column.name: assigned_to_experience
per_column.rationale: Agent experience would be a strong explanatory axis for why some agents are slower — highly relevant. But the table contains no experience/tenure information; the near-uniform 0..N ramp distribution and constant 0/1 values on samples indicate a fabricated or index-based synthetic value not derivable from the source.

per_column.name: category_incident_count
per_column.rationale: Category workload/volume could plausibly relate to resolution time, so conceptually useful. However the smooth 0,1,2,3... ramp and per-row values (all 0 on Infrastructure samples) do not correspond to any aggregable count grounded in the table; appears to be an invented/index-like value.

judge.rationale: The added columns target the right constructs for the query (resolution duration, priority/criticality, category, agent experience, category volume). However groundedness is the major weakness: the core resolution_hours is miscomputed with impossible negative values, and assigned_to_experience and category_incident_count assert quantities with no supporting field in the source, showing telltale synthetic ramp distributions. priority_numeric, category_type, and is_critical are well grounded; is_critical is somewhat redundant with priority.
